title: Product Marketing Manager
description:
Description
Sentra is the AI Data Readiness platform for enterprises deploying AI at scale. Sentra continuously discovers, classifies, and governs sensitive data across cloud, SaaS, data warehouses, and AI environments - giving security teams complete visibility into what AI systems can access, what they can expose, and where compliance violations exist. Unlike alternatives that copy data to vendor clouds or require customer-managed outpost infrastructure, Sentra provisions ephemeral scanners directly inside the customer's environment, delivering petabyte-scale classification at a fraction of the cost. Trusted by Lyft, SoFi, Munich RE, PennyMac, Glovo, and others.
We’re hiring a Product Marketing Manager who can turn complex technology into clear, differentiated stories that resonate with customers and help our field teams win.
﻿About The Role
We’re hiring a Senior Product Marketing Manager who can turn complex technology into clear, differentiated stories that resonate with customers and help our field teams win.
This is a highly visible, hands-on individual contributor role with significant ownership across positioning and messaging, competitive intelligence, product launches, and sales enablement. You’ll work closely with Product, Sales, Customer Success, and the broader Marketing team to shape how we bring our platform and capabilities to market and how we communicate Sentra ’s value throughout the buyer journey.
You’ll be comfortable going deep with technical teams, engaging directly with customers and sellers, and turning what you learn into simple, compelling messaging that differentiates Sentra in the market.
Responsibilities
Positioning & Messaging
Help lead and evolve positioning and messaging across Sentra ’s platform, products, and key use cases. Translate complex technical capabilities into clear, differentiated customer value and ensure our messaging resonates with both technical and business audiences.
﻿Competitive Intelligence
Scale our competitive intelligence program, including competitive positioning, battlecards, objection handling, and field guidance. Stay close to the market and our sales organization to understand how competitors are positioning, where we win and lose, and what our field teams need to navigate competitive opportunities.
﻿Product Launches & GTM
Lead product launches and key GTM initiatives, partnering cross-functionally with Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Marketing to develop messaging, enablement, launch plans, and execution. Ensure teams understand not only what we’re launching, but why it matters to customers and how to take it to market.
﻿Sales Enablement
Create the messaging, tools, and training our field teams need to sell effectively. Partner closely with Sales to understand what resonates with buyers, where deals get stuck, and where additional messaging, competitive intelligence, or enablement can improve execution.
Customer & Market Insights
Stay close to customers, prospects, sellers, and the broader market to understand evolving needs, buying drivers, objections, and trends. Bring those insights back into Product, Marketing, and GTM decisions and help ensure the voice of the customer is reflected in our strategy and messaging.
﻿Content & Thought Leadership
Partner with the broader Marketing team and executives to translate Sentra ’s point of view into compelling content, campaigns, customer stories, and thought leadership. Help make complex data security and AI challenges understandable and relevant to our target audiences.
Requirements

• 5+ years of B2B cybersecurity product marketing experience in data, cloud, or enterprise software

• Demonstrated ownership of positioning and messaging for complex technical products

• Strong experience in competitive intelligence, sales enablement, and translating market insights into actionable field guidance

• Proven experience leading product launches and cross-functional GTM programs

• Ability to understand complex technology

title: Delivery Capacity & Demand Manager (f/m/x)
description:
About the role: What's in the Box

Every day, a defined set of rules decides what every new HelloFresh customer sees: a unique mix of delivery days, prices and recommended selections. Your job, should you choose to accept it, is to keep that rule-set correct in a constantly moving environment: configuring it, checking it daily, documenting it, and fixing exceptions before a misconfiguration reaches a customer or a warehouse. 

You'll join Demand Steering , the team within Network Operations Europe that shapes those offerings so they add up to a plan our warehouses and logistics partners can actually execute. That means balancing what customers want against the real constraints of the journey from click to delivery: every box still has to be produced in a shift at a production facility and delivered by a van on a route.

Using our in-house demand steering tool, you'll configure the delivery offering customers see at checkout across your own set of European markets: which delivery days and time windows are offered, at what price, with which recommendation, and to which customer segment. As technical owner of that configuration, you'll balance demand against capacity: working with supply chain planners, local market teams and our tech partners to validate holiday shifts and peak periods, check daily that the offering behaved as intended, and catch misconfigurations before a customer or a warehouse feels them..

What you’ll do: The Recipe

• Own the delivery proposition for your set of European markets: the delivery days, time windows, cut-offs, pricing nudges and recommendations customers see when they place or change an order.

• Configure and calibrate our in-house demand steering tool, so demand is guided towards the capacity we have rather than blocked outright when a production site or delivery route fills up.

• Monitor daily whether the offering ran as expected across your markets, and get to the bottom of it when it didn't: a data pipeline that stalled, a setting that's off, or a shift in how customers are behaving.

• Dig into the data with SQL and our monitoring dashboards to establish what actually happened,.

• Make it make sense to turn technical outcomes into a clear story for colleagues who don't live inside the tool.

• Partner with supply chain planners, logistics teams, local market colleagues and our tech partners to translate their constraints into configurations, and to flag early where a forecast and a delivery plan are heading for a collision.

• Lead the validation for holiday shifts and peak periods, giving a clear go/no-go recommendation backed by evidence rather than instinct.

• Shape where the tool goes next, improving the configurations, checks and documentation that keep demand steering reliable as we roll the model out across more markets.

What you’ll bring: The Ingredients

• Experience in logistics, supply chain, operations or a related field, where you've seen how a change to what you offer customers affects their journey

• Confidence with data: you write your own SQL queries, work comfortably in spreadsheets, and read a dashboard closely enough to tell a real signal from noise.

• A methodical way of working: you like things documented and done properly, and you stay effective while the system around you is still being built out.

• The ability to explain a technical problem to a non-technical colleague, and to make a recommendation land with evidence behind it.

• An appetite for ownership over the long haul: you'd rather take one system and develop true mastery in it than move from project to project.

• Fluent English, and you're based in Berlin or ready to move there.

Above all, we are looking for people who will make HelloFresh better. There are many different ways of developing skills, and we love diverse experiences! So even if you don’t “tick all the boxes” but think you’d thrive in this role, we would really like to learn more about you.

What we offer: The Toppings

Elevate yo

title: Sr. Manager, International Programs
description:
This role is for someone who delivers results across borders, time zones, and organizational boundaries. We are looking for a hands-on operator who personally drives complex, high-stakes engagements to successful outcomes, not someone who manages program governance from a distance.

Tomorrow.io's Customer Delivery and Operations team sits at the center of the company, connecting our business units to the technical organization. We own the full lifecycle of customer programs across our global portfolio, from pre-sale technical engagement and proof of concept through post-sale delivery and operational support. This role will span a diverse set of international programs, national agencies, and other large-scale organizations operating in demanding, mission-critical environments.

You will own programs end to end. That means having command of every detail: the contract terms, the technical requirements, the stakeholder map, the risks, and the critical path forward. You will be expected to identify and resolve blockers proactively, close gaps between customer expectations and delivery, and maintain momentum across multiple concurrent engagements in different countries and contexts.

You will join a small, high-output team in a fast-moving company where the operating model is still maturing. There is no large program office behind you. You will be expected to build the frameworks and processes you need, not wait for them to be handed to you. The right candidate sees that as an opportunity, not a limitation.

What Winning Looks Like

• Your programs deliver on time, within scope, and with zero surprises to leadership or the customer. Contract milestones are tracked, invoicing is clean, and compliance artifacts are complete without being chased.

• Customers in your programs trust you personally, not just the company. They come to you directly when something needs attention because you have earned that access through consistent follow-through.

• Internal teams (Science, Product, Engineering, Legal) treat your programs as well-run and easy to support because you bring clear requirements, realistic timelines, and full context, not last-minute fire drills.

• You run multiple concurrent programs across different countries, customer types, and regulatory environments without dropping threads. Each one has a clear status, a clear next step, and a clear owner for every open item.

• When a new international opportunity enters the pipeline, you can step into the pre-sale engagement to support deal reviews, scope proofs of concept, and ensure the technical and financial picture is solid before we commit.

• Risks surface early. You identify issues before they escalate and bring proposed mitigations alongside the diagnosis.

• You raise the bar for the teams around you. Business Development and Sales teams produce stronger scoping because you challenge them to think through requirements before engaging the technical organization. Your programs become the reference point for what well-run delivery looks like.

What You'll Own

Program Delivery

• Own and drive the full lifecycle of international programs: contract kickoff, solution delivery, proof of concept execution, operational deployment, and ongoing support.

• Translate signed contracts into executable program plans with defined milestones, deliverables, ownership, and accountability, and drive follow-through across all stakeholders.

• Manage scope, schedule, budget, and technical risk across multiple concurrent programs in diverse operational and regulatory environments.

• Ensure all contract deliverables, including documentation, reporting, invoicing, and compliance artifacts, are completed accurately and on time.

Stakeholder Management

• Serve as the primary point of contact for customers on active programs. Build direct relationships with decision-makers and technical counterparts across organizations and geographies.

• Drive alignment across internal teams: Legal, Finance, Prod

title: Head of Pharmacovigilance
description:
Location:   This position may be performed remotely, but requires the flexibility and willingness to travel as needed.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Head of Clinical Sciences, the Head of Pharmacovigilance (PV) is a physician who builds and leads Praxis’s in-house pharmacovigilance function across clinical development and commercial products. Praxis is building its pharmacovigilance system in-house rather than outsourcing it, and is using an AI-enabled safety database to create an efficient case-handling process. The Head of PV owns that system and the team that runs it.

The function is organized in two parts. Pharmacovigilance for programs in clinical development is led by the PV Clinical Development Lead, who reports to the Head of PV, leads a dedicated clinical trial safety team, and carries day-to-day medical safety oversight of the clinical-stage portfolio. Pharmacovigilance for commercial products is held directly by the Head of PV, who is personally accountable for postmarketing safety surveillance, reporting, and benefit-risk, and who directly leads the commercial-product Medical Reviewer and PV Scientist. The PV Operations Lead supports both parts of the function. Across both, the Head of PV is accountable for the pharmacovigilance system as a whole, sets the standards and governance that the two parts operate under, and is the final safety decision-maker for the company.

The safety database will already be built and validated. What this role takes on is a system that needs enhancement and modification as new products advance and launch, a quality system that has to keep pace with it, and a team that has to be assembled and qualified. The Head of PV understands pharmacovigilance operations well enough to direct them and to judge whether they are working, but does not carry them personally; the PV Operations Lead is engaged for that and is involved throughout.

The role is accountable, not advisory. The Head of PV owns the pharmacovigilance system, expedited and periodic reporting compliance, the conclusions and submission of the aggregate safety reports, and the integrity of the signal management process, and defends them to health authorities. As the senior safety physician, the Head of PV personally holds the medical determinations that sit at the center of the function for commercial products, and holds final authority over those made for clinical development programs: benefit-risk, signal adjudication, and complex case causality. The Head of PV works collaboratively with Clinical Development, Clinical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Medical Affairs, Data Science, and Commercial to ensure comprehensive safety oversight of Praxis products.

 

Primary Responsibilities

Leadership of the PV Function

• Lead the pharmacovigilance function as a whole, accountable for the pharmacovigilance system, its quality, and its compliance across clinical development and commercial products.

• Directly lead pharmacovigilance for commercial products, including the commercial-product Medical Reviewer and PV Scientist, holding personal accountability for postmarketing safety surveillance, expedited and periodic reporting, signal management, and benefit-risk.

• Oversee pharmacovigilance for clinical development programs through the PV Clinical Development Lead and the clinical trial safety team reporting to that role: set expectations, standards, and escalation criteria; review the safety positions taken; and retain final authority over program-significant safety decisions.

• Ensure the clinical development and commercial parts of the function operate as one system, with a single quality system, a single safety database, consistent medical judgment across both teams, and a clean handover of safety accountability as products move from development to market.

Senior Medical Determinations

• Make and articulate the benefit-risk determination for each commercial product in aggregate rep

title: Business Development / Mba Co-Founder (F/M/D) Role At Startup Chillquanta
description:
**CHILLQUANTA
**Bochum, Germany (Ruhr University Bochum) | On-site / Hybrid | Co-Founder / Equity | Deep Tech / Quantum & Semiconductor Metrology
**About ChillQuanta
**ChillQuanta is developing an electro-optic spectrometer for inspecting and characterizing photonic qubits (semiconductor quantum-dot single- and entangled-photon sources), aiming to replace or combine today's separate methods (capacitance-voltage, photoluminescence, resonance fluorescence spectroscopy) with one new sub-100-femtosecond-resolution, non-destructive electro-optic technique - with a patent filing already in progress. Target market: quantum and semiconductor chip makers.
**The opportunity
**Founded by Amar Alok (CEO, PhD in Experimental Physics from RUB, 4+ years in ultrafast optics and pump-probe spectroscopy) alongside a Chemistry postdoc, ChillQuanta has a lab prototype (TRL 3-4) benchmarked against single-atom data, an Invention Disclosure accepted by RUB (April 2026) with a manuscript in preparation for Physical Review Letters, and over €12k raised so far. The next step is turning the lab prototype into an automated instrument and deciding between licensing and starting a company - which is where a business co-founder comes in. ChillQuanta is separately also open to an AI/ML co-founder to help build wafer-scale AI prediction capability.
Tasks
What you will own
**Company build-up & strategy
**- Help decide and execute the path from lab prototype to company: licensing vs. start-up, incorporation, and go-to-market strategy for the quantum/semiconductor metrology market.
- Own fundraising strategy and investor relations as ChillQuanta moves beyond its initial ~€12k raised.
**Commercialization
**- Turn the lab prototype (TRL 3-4) into an automated, sellable instrument in partnership with the technical team.
- Build relationships with semiconductor and quantum chip makers as early customers

description:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge.  Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking an Electrical Commissioning Engineer to execute the buildout, startup, and handover of electrical systems for SpaceXAI's high-performance data centers. This is a hands-on role where you will commission, test, troubleshoot, and turn over critical systems that support next-generation AI supercomputing infrastructure.

You will work closely with construction, engineering, operations, EPC contractors, and OEM vendors to deliver safe, reliable, and high-quality electrical systems. This is a full-time, onsite role with travel to SpaceXAI data center construction sites across the United States.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Execute all electrical commissioning activities for MV/LV switchgear, generators, UPS systems, PDUs, ATS/STS, transformers, relays, busway, and associated controls in hyperscale data center environments.

• Execute functional performance testing, pre-functional testing, site acceptance testing, load-bank testing, protection-relay testing, integrated system testing, and system turnover to operations.

• Maintain comprehensive as-built documentation, test records, issue logs, and final commissioning reports.

• Support and deliver training programs for operations and maintenance teams on commissioned systems.

• Participate in constructability reviews, design feedback sessions, and lessons-learned meetings to continuously improve installation quality and future project execution.

• Support commissioning schedules and punch-list resolution to meet aggressive project timelines.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering.

• 5+ years of experience in commissioning for electrical systems.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Working knowledge of commissioning test equipment (power analyzers, insulation testers, hipot testers, torque tools, IR cameras, load banks, relay test sets, etc.), or demonstrated aptitude to learn it in the field.

• Familiarity with relevant codes and standards (NEC, NFPA 70/70B/70E, IEEE, NETA, NESC, Uptime Institute).

• Ability to read, interpret, and redline electrical drawings, one-lines, three-lines, control schematics, and sequence of operations; update as-built models after commissioning.

• Experience coordinating with multi-discipline teams, contractors, and vendors in construction environments.

• Ability to work safely in industrial construction environments and follow LOTO, NFPA, OSHA, and SpaceXAI safety protocols.

ABOUT CODERABBIT

CodeRabbit is the leading AI code review platform, trusted by more than 17,000 customers and 150,000 open-source projects, conducting over 2 million code reviews each week. We build the symbiotic partnership between developers and AI that makes shipping fast software safe again, reviewing every pull request, IDE change, and CLI commit so teams can move quickly without breaking things.

 

We are a fast-moving, well-funded company, fresh off a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation - building Agentic Change Management, the control layer for software changes created by humans and agents. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.

THE OPPORTUNITY

CodeRabbit helps engineering teams trust the code their AI agents write. We want the same confidence in our own numbers. As our Senior Data Analyst, you’ll build the dashboards and reports that give leadership strategic insight across Finance, Revenue, Marketing and Product. You’ll launch our foundational BI tool, then build the agentic workflows that model our data and generate new dashboards and insights on request. You’ll join a small Business Systems team that builds with frontier AI tools every day.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Launch our foundational BI tool and build the first exec and team dashboards on it.

- Build exec- and board-level reporting for Finance and GTM, including ARR waterfalls, pipeline, funnel and deal risk.

- Run deep-dive analyses on the gaps between targets and actuals, pipeline health, margins, and billing issues.

- Build and maintain dbt models that form a governed data layer, so people and agents can query with confidence.

- Identify gaps in our data warehouse, ETL pipelines, and semantic layer to enforce canonical definitions and shared metrics across the business.

- Build and maintain the context layer and agentic harness that let anyone at CodeRabbit generate dashboards and insights on request, with tests and review before anything ships.

- Work as a collaborative partner to Finance and GTM: understand their problems and needs, then build workflows and data products that scale with our teams.

QUALIFICATIONS

- 3+ years as a data analyst or senior data analyst, ideally at a high-growth B2B SaaS company.

- Strong SQL and hands-on experience with a cloud data warehouse such as BigQuery or Snowflake.

- Experience building and maintaining dbt models and the semantic layer.

- Experience building dashboards and self-serve analytics in a modern BI tool such as Omni, Sigma or Looker.

- Working knowledge of finance and GTM metrics: ARR, net and gross retention, bookings, pipeline coverage, CAC and gross margin, and how a forecast miss gets traced to its causes.

- Real experience using agentic tools such as Claude Code or Codex for analysis and for building, with something you built that you can show us.

- Comfortable working with messy data and understanding trade-offs when drawing insights.

- Ability to work and communicate with senior leadership, and technical and non-technical peers.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Familiarity with ETL and ELT pipelines, orchestration tools (such as Airflow, Dagster or Fivetran) and reverse ETL.

- Experience at an AI company or early-stage startup, where definitions change and you build the first version of everything.

- Experience with CRMs like Salesforce and billing systems like Chargebee

- Python or TypeScript, Git and code review, or a dashboards-as-code tool such as Evidence, Streamlit or Observable.

- Experience building agent tooling: MCP servers, an agent harness, or CI for analytics code.

title: Senior Product Designer – Toast Retail
description:
Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy. 

Toast is making it faster and easier for retailers to get started on Toast: the path from a store's existing product data to a correctly configured, actively selling location. We are seeking a highly skilled, AI-native Senior Product Designer to lead that experience: someone with a strong portfolio, a track record of leading design for complex product areas, a focus on exceptional UI design, and the hands-on ability to build working prototypes with AI tools like Replit, Magic Patterns, or Claude. This role involves designing for the unique needs of a diverse retail customer base, including convenience stores, bottle shops, grocery stores, hybrid models, and beyond.

You will lead design for Toast Retail's Experience Platform team, working day to day with product and engineering partners in our Dublin office and the U.S., and reporting to Toast Retail's design leadership in the U.S. Together you will turn product strategy into the setup and onboarding experiences that make retailers feel Toast is built for them.

Why This Role Matters

A retailer's first 90 days on Toast decide whether they stay. Before a store can sell, thousands of items need clean names, categories, brands, pack sizes, taxes, deposits, age restrictions, and images, and most of that data arrives messy, from another system or a spreadsheet. The experiences you design will decide how quickly a new store goes live, how much of that work Toast can do for them, and whether the people setting up the store, often owners juggling a business that is already open, feel in control or buried in it.

You will be Toast Retail's design presence in our Dublin office: the on-site design partner for its product and engineering teams, and part of Toast's wider design community. As a senior designer working across regions and time zones, you will set design direction for your area with a high degree of autonomy: keeping local teams unblocked, making well-informed design and scope tradeoffs within the broader product vision, shaping the roadmap alongside your product and engineering partners, and bringing US-based design, product, and business stakeholders in when direction, customer impact, or strategic choices need broader alignment.

A day in the life (Responsibilities) 

• Lead design for your product area: Take your area from early discovery through shipped UI, set its design direction and quality bar, and connect each workflow to the broader Toast Retail vision. Help shape what the team builds, not only how it looks.

• Prototype with AI: Use AI prototyping tools such as Replit, Magic Patterns, or Claude to build working, interactive prototypes with realistic data, so ideas can be tested with customers and engineers before the team commits to them. Use AI across the rest of your practice too, from synthesizing research to exploring concepts, validating outputs carefully and modeling responsible, secure use of AI for the team.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

JOIN US IF YOU WANT TO

1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

Lendable is launching its credit card product in Mexico and building a founding

local team. We're looking for someone to own the day-to-day operation of that

product: the customer conversations, yes, but also the queues, the exceptions,

the data behind them, and the tooling that makes all of it faster next month

than it was this month.

This is not a scripted support seat. Our support stack is heavily instrumented

and increasingly AI-assisted, which means the routine answers are largely

handled what's left is the interesting part: cases that don't fit the script,

patterns nobody has noticed yet, and processes that still need a human to design

them. You'll spend part of your week talking to customers and part of it

figuring out why they had to contact us at all.

We're a small team in a market we're still learning. The person who does well

here is curious, comfortable being the one who doesn't wait to be told, and

happy to wear whichever hat the day needs.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

1. Own the daily operational queues, end to end

title: Lead-Producer Services Readiness
description:
Role Overview

The Producer Services Readiness Lead serves as the senior Producer Services subject matter expert for translating approved requirements into practical workflows, standard operating procedures, training, service processes, controls, and launch plans. The role leads and coordinates readiness activities for new and changing business-process requirements within Producer Services.

The Lead applies sound operational judgment and escalates decisions involving policy, risk, resources, or cross-functional ownership to the appropriate Producer Services leader. The Lead coordinates readiness activities and assesses whether staff, workflows, materials, system dependencies, and escalation paths have been prepared before new producer-facing requirements go live, escalating unresolved readiness risks as appropriate.

The role provides targeted onboarding and Support readiness during launches and peak periods but does not become the standing owner of routine onboarding, Support production, regulatory interpretation, or technical delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Business Process Readiness & Subject Matter Expertise

• Serve as the Producer Services subject matter expert for the implementation of new and changing business-process requirements.

• Translate approved policy, program, regulatory, financial, and operational decisions into clear Producer Services workflows and operating requirements.

• Develop and recommend how approved requirements should be executed across affected Producer Services teams, working with team leaders to confirm the final operating approach.

• Map current- and future-state processes, including roles, handoffs, decision rights, controls, exceptions, and escalation paths.

• Identify missing decisions, process gaps, conflicting requirements, and dependencies that could prevent successful implementation.

• Recommend practical operating approaches that balance producer clarity, control requirements, service quality, and available capacity for review and approval by Producer Services leadership.

• Maintain awareness of new and changing Producer Services processes across registration, reporting, validation, adjustments, corrections, payments, delinquency, and regulator referrals to support readiness planning and implementation activities.

• Process Implementation & Operationalization

• Assess the operational feasibility and impacts of new or changing requirements affecting Producer Services.

• Coordinate and support the implementation and operationalization of approved Producer Services processes, partnering with process owners and functional leaders to ensure readiness activities are completed.

• Draft and maintain operational process documentation, including SOPs, process maps, job aids, checklists, decision trees, intake procedures, queue-routing rules, and escalation protocols.

• Document process ownership, handoffs, decision rights, and escalation paths across Producer Services and partner functions.

• Coordinate the transition of approved requirements from process design into day-to-day operations.

• Assess readiness and identify gaps related to workflows, documentation, controls, staffing, data, knowledge, and escalation paths before launch, escalating unresolved risks to the appropriate leader.

• Monitor adoption after launch, identify operational gaps, and coordinate approved process updates, training activities, or corrective actions with the appropriate process owners.

• Transition implemented processes to the appropriate steady-state owner after stabilization.

Training, Launch & Adoption

• Develop and coordinate operational training for new and changing Producer Services processes.

• Prepare facilitator materials, staff job aids, process guidance, scenarios, and readiness resources.

• Facilitate or support training sessions for Producer Services and other affected teams.

• Support readiness activities designed to ensure affected staff have access to process guidance, resources,

description:

We are seeking a Senior Technical Consultant to lead firewall, network access control, and SASE engagements across diverse enterprise environments. This role spans three core technology pillars: next-generation firewall design and deployment (Cisco Secure Firewall, Palo Alto Networks), Cisco ISE-based network access control and identity services, and SASE/Zero Trust architectures (Zscaler, Palo Alto Prisma Access, Cisco Secure Access, Netskope).

The ideal candidate combines deep hands-on expertise across these platforms with strong consulting skills, owning end-to-end delivery from discovery and design through implementation, testing, and knowledge transfer. This is a client-facing role that requires the ability to lead technical workstreams, produce professional documentation, and communicate complex security strategies to both technical and executive audiences.

Key Responsibilities: Firewall

• Design and deploy Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) managed by Firewall Management Center (FMC), including high-availability pairs, threat policies (Snort IPS, malware defense, URL filtering), and both site-to-site and remote access VPN configurations.

• Configure and manage Palo Alto Networks next-generation firewalls running PAN-OS, including security profiles (Antivirus, Anti-Spyware, Vulnerability Protection, WildFire), App-ID, User-ID, SSL/TLS decryption, and centralized management via Panorama.

• Lead firewall migration projects including legacy Cisco ASA to FTD conversions, cross-vendor migrations (Check Point, Fortinet, Juniper to Palo Alto or Cisco), and policy translation with rule optimization during cutover.

• Design network segmentation architectures using firewall zones, virtual routers, VRFs, and policy-based routing to enforce least-privilege east-west and north-south traffic controls.

• Deploy cloud-native firewall solutions including Palo Alto Cloud NGFW for AWS and Azure, and Cisco Secure Firewall Cloud Native for containerized and cloud workload environments.

• Implement firewall high availability designs including active/standby failover, active/active clustering, and multi-context deployments for service provider and large enterprise environments.

• Configure centralized logging, SIEM integration (Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, syslog), and NetFlow/IPFIX for traffic analytics, threat correlation, and compliance reporting.

• Perform firewall rule base optimization, policy cleanup, and compliance auditing to reduce attack surface and align with regulatory frameworks (PCI-DSS, HIPAA, NIST).

• Integrate Cisco Secure Firewall with Cisco XDR for cross-platform threat detection, event correlation, and automated incident response across the security portfolio.

• Automate firewall provisioning, configuration backup, and policy deployment using infrastructure-as-code tools (Terraform, Ansible) and vendor APIs for repeatable, auditable workflows.

• Deploy Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) for wired and wireless authentication, MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB), and RADIUS/TACACS+ device administration across campus, branch, and data

title: Solutions Architect
description:
Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model - which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

The Role

Every Celonis outcome starts with data. As a Solutions Architect, you make sure our customers’ data gets into the Celonis Platform reliably, securely, and at scale, and that insights and actions flow back out into the systems and AI tools where work actually happens.

You’ll join our customer programs team as one of the first technical faces of Celonis. You’ll work hands-on across the full integration toolkit: deploying our out-of-the-box extractors, building custom API connectors in a low-code environment, writing code for push-based ingestion, connecting Celonis to customer lakehouses and LLMs, and configuring writebacks, SSO, and user provisioning. Part implementation consultant, part integration engineer, part trusted technical advisor, this role is ideal for someone early in their career who wants broad exposure to enterprise architecture and modern data and AI integration patterns.

What You’ll Do

Data integration and ingestion

• Implement standard extractors. Install, configure, and troubleshoot Celonis out-of-the-box extractors in customer landscapes, including SAP (ECC and S/4HANA), JDBC-based databases, and cloud applications such as Salesforce, ServiceNow, and others.

• Build custom API connectors. Design and build custom connectors with Celonis Extractor Builder for source systems that expose data through REST or SOAP APIs, handling authentication (OAuth 2.0, API keys, certificates), pagination, rate limits, and incremental (delta) loads.

• Enable push-based ingestion. Help customers design and develop scripts and pipelines (typically in Python) that push data to Celonis via the Data Ingestion API, and advise on file formats, scheduling, and error handling.

• Connect to the lakehouse. Set up zero-copy data sharing between Celonis and customer lakehouses such as Databricks and Microsoft Fabric, including Delta Sharing configuration, access controls, and data freshness.

Actions, AI, and platform connectivity

• Close the loop with writebacks. Configure Action Flows and other integration patterns that write back to customer systems (for example, updating records in SAP, Salesforce, or ticketing tools) so Celonis insights turn into action.

• Connect Celonis to AI. Help customers connect Celonis to their LLMs and AI agents through MCP, covering authentication, permissions, and governance.

Identity, security, and governance

• Own authentication and provisioning. Configure SSO (SAML, OIDC) with identity providers such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, and Ping, and set up SCIM-based user and group provisioning.

• Be the security translator. Support customer security, privacy, and compliance reviews, explain the Celonis architecture and data flows, and advise on topics like data minimization, pseudonymization, and least-privilege access.

Customer and team impact

• Scope with confidence. Run technical discovery, document integration architectures and requirements, and estimate effort so projects start on solid footing.

• Be the voice of the field. Escalate product gaps and bugs with clear, reproducible detail, and share field feedback that shapes our integration roadmap.

At Render, we’re building the modern cloud platform for developers creating AI-native, full-stack, multi-service applications. Our mission is to eliminate the tradeoff between the power of hyperscalers and the simplicity of developer-friendly platforms-so teams can ship fast, scale reliably, and focus on their product, not infrastructure.

Unlike complex hyperscalers or ephemeral edge/serverless solutions, Render offers a developer-first experience with persistent compute, dynamic autoscaling, built-in orchestration, and observability, allowing teams to launch, scale, and manage real-world applications without writing infrastructure code or managing servers. Whether you're building LLM-powered applications, scalable SaaS products, or async processing pipelines, Render empowers teams to move fast and scale confidently from MVP to millions of users.

Our platform is trusted by over 7 million developers worldwide and continues to grow rapidly. In February 2026, we raised an additional $100M in Series C financing, bringing our total funding to $260M, to accelerate our vision of making cloud infrastructure both powerful and intuitive-designed for the speed of modern AI development.

We’re a diverse and talented team that values craft, velocity, and user experience. If you’re excited to help shape the future of the intelligent cloud and empower developers everywhere, we’d love to hear from you.

APPLYING TO RENDER

We're seeking candidates who possess high integrity, humility, and an insatiable drive to learn. Through reasoned discussions and continuous feedback, we strive to improve both individually and collectively. We foster an environment of mutual trust and respect, empowering effective debate to achieve the best outcomes for our customers and team.

We're looking for a Staff/Principal Founding Design Systems Lead to build that judgment into Render's foundations.

This isn't about maintaining a component library. It's about enabling designers, engineers, and agents to build experiences that look, feel, and work like Render, without a designer making every decision or the design systems team reviewing every change. At a company whose whole promise is a platform that just works, the design system is how we keep craft scaling as the product and the team grows.

This role starts hands-on. You're a designer first, with the technical depth to get into the code. You'll partner with the Head of Design to set the vision, then do the foundational work yourself: decide where or whether our Figma library lives and how it operates, get deep into what an AI-ready design system really means, and prototype, test, and ship the system in code. As the function grows, you'll build and lead the team around it. You're energized by building from the ground up, not inheriting something finished.

title: Data Scientist: Product
locationText: Austin, Texas, United States; New York +4 more
description:
About Thatch

For most people, health insurance is something that happens to them: a plan chosen by someone else, with little room to fit their life. Thatch is changing that. We help companies give every employee a real healthcare budget instead of a one-size-fits-all plan, so people can choose the coverage and care that works for them, and employers get predictable costs they can control.

It’s a simple idea, but making it real means solving hard problems across healthcare, payments, and technology, and we’re just getting started. We look for people who like solving complex problems, use good judgment, and are comfortable working through ambiguity. People here care deeply about our customers, take real responsibility for what gets built, and are driven by doing work that matters.

About the role

Thatch is changing how health benefits work. We're building software that makes it easier for businesses to offer health coverage and gives employees more choice and control.

We're looking for a Data Scientist to help our Product and Operations teams understand how people use Thatch and where we can make the biggest impact. You'll own the data models and metrics behind our product, from plan shopping and enrollment to reimbursements and everyday benefit usage.

You'll dig into user behavior, uncover friction, and design experiments that help us decide what to build and improve next. This is a hands-on role where you'll build the analytics foundation teams rely on, turn complex data into clear recommendations, and help shape our product strategy.

What you will do

• Partner with Product and Operations to answer important questions and inform product priorities.

• Define and own product metrics, from company-wide success measures to feature-level performance.

• Analyze user journeys, engagement, and operational data to uncover friction and opportunities.

• Design and evaluate experiments to measure the impact of product changes.

• Build and maintain dbt models, metrics, dashboards, and analytical tools that teams rely on.

• Improve data quality, instrumentation, and self-serve analytics so teams can make confident decisions.

What we are looking for

• Experience using analytics, data science, and experimentation to influence product decisions.

• Strong SQL skills and experience with dbt or similar data transformation tools.

• Experience building analytical data models and dashboards using BI or visualization tools.

• Proficiency in Python for analysis, experimentation, or statistical modeling.

• Strong product judgment and the ability to turn complex findings into clear, actionable recommendations.

• Comfortable working independently, navigating ambiguity, and partnering across teams. 

Tools and tech stack

• Data: Snowflake, SQL, dbt

• Analytics: Omni, Hex, Python

• Development: GitHub, CI/CD

• AI: Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, and other tools that help us work faster and smarter

You won't work directly in our application layer day-to-day, but familiarity with source data and event instrumentation from systems like Ruby on Rails is helpful.

Experience that stands out

• Influencing product roadmaps and prioritization through data.

• Building experimentation practices, including guardrail metrics, sample-size guidance, or analysis frameworks.

• Analyzing funnels, retention, cohorts, or engagement across complex user journeys.

• Building statistical or machine-learning models for segmentation, forecasting, propensity, or recommendations.

• Experience in healthcare, fintech, or other regulated industries.

What to expect

We aim to move quickly, and most candidates complete the process within 2-3 weeks. You can expect:

• An initial conversation with a recruiter.

• A conversation with the hiring manager and a lightweight Python coding exercise.

• A take-home analytics exercise.

• A review of your work, a data modeling and metrics exercise with the team, and a discussion with cross-functional partners.
